m: regarding His statement, When kings enter a town, they corrupt it, and she said: If this man’s only concern is the world, then we will satisfy him, and if he only wants religion, then he will not say anything other than that,
h
And I am sending to them a gift

and seeing with what the messengers return. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Bilqis was a clever, well-mannered woman in a royal house. She only ruled for a few days, and her family had passed away. She ruled and was ruled until she was made ruler. Her religion and the religion of her people, as has been mentioned, were heretics. When she read the letter, she heard a letter that was not from the letters of the kings who came before her. So she sent to the people of Yemen to consult, and she said to them: “O eminent ones, indeed a noble letter has been delivered to me. It is from Solomon, and it is: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Do not exalt yourselves over me, but come to me in submission.” To His saying:
h
With what do the messengers return

? Then she said: “A letter has come to me, the like of which has not come to me from any king before him. If the man is a prophet sent, then we have no power or strength against him. But if the man is a king who boasts, then he is more powerful than us, and I cannot count.” She prepared gifts from the kind of things given to kings, from the things they issue fatwas about, and she said: If he is a king, he will accept the gift and desire the money, but if he is a prophet, he has no need of this world and does not want it. He only wants us to enter into his religion with him and follow his commands, or something like that.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And indeed, I am sending to them a gift, that he sent male and female slaves, who were wearing the same clothing. She said: If a separation is made between them so that the male is known from the female, then he returns the gift, then he is a prophet, and we should follow him and enter his religion. So Solomon separated the male and female slaves, and returned the gift, and said: Do you provide me with wealth while what God has given me is better than what He has given you?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: Among the gifts that were sent were slave girls and maids who differed in their clothing, so that the boys could be distinguished from the slave girls. He said: So he called for water and the slave girls performed ablution from the elbows down, and the boys performed ablution from the elbows up. He said: My father used to narrate this hadith to us.

c: Abdul-A’la told us, he said: Marwan bin Mu’awiyah told us, he said: Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: And I am sending them a gift. He said: I sent a brick of gold, and she said: If he wants this world, I will teach him, and if he wants the Hereafter, I will teach him. And His statement,
h
So let us consider with what means the messengers will return

, meaning: So let us consider with what good deeds and actions he will take in My gift that I sent to him. Will he accept it and turn away from us, or will he reject the gift and persist in demanding that we follow him in his religion? The alif was dropped from ma in His statement, with and its original form is with because when the Arabs say ma in the meaning of which, and then connect it to a preposition, they drop its alif to differentiate it from the question and other things, as God, the Most High, said, About what are they asking one another?
r
(An-Naba’: 1)
, They said, “In what were you?
r
(An-Nisa’: 97)

, and sometimes they keep the alif in it, as the poet said: Why did he curse me, you mean person, like a pig wallowing in the dirt? She said, And I am sent to them, and she was sent to Solomon alone, in the manner that we explained in His statement, for fear of Pharaoh and his chiefs
r
(Yunus 10:83)

evidence.text: When she read the letter, she heard a letter that was not from the letters of the kings who came before her.

x: And His statement,
h
So when Solomon came
, he said, 'Do you provide me with wealth?' If someone were to say, How was it said, '
h
So when Solomon came
,' making the report about Solomon's coming from one person? And He had already said, Then consider
h
with what the messengers will return
. If the messenger was one person, then how could it be said,
h
With what the messengers will return
? And if they were a group, then how could it be said,
h
So when Solomon came

?" It was said that this is similar to what we have already explained, that the Arabs express the report of a matter that was from one person in the manner of a report from a group, if the report is not intended to be about one specific person who is specifically referred to, so it is named in the report. And it was said that the messenger whom the Queen of Sheba sent to Solomon was one person, so that is why He said, "
h
So when Solomon came
," meaning: When the messenger came to Solomon.

And those who said that proved the correctness of what they said from that by Solomon's saying to the messenger, "Return to them. And it was mentioned that that in Abdullah's reading, So when they came to Solomon is in the plural, and that is because of the wording of His statement,
h
With what the messengers will return

." So the plural is suitable for the wording and the singular for the meaning. And his saying, He said, ‘Do you provide me with money?’ means: Solomon said when the messenger came from the woman with her gifts: Do you provide me with money? The reciters differed in their recitation of this word.
Some of the reciters from Medina recited it atamdudunni with two nuns and with the yaa added.
Some of the Kufians recited it in the same way, except that they deleted the yaa from the end of it and broke the final nun.
Some of the reciters from Basra recited it with two nuns and with the yaa added when connected and deleted it when stopped.

Some of the reciters from Kufa recited it with a shaddah on the nun and with the yaa added. All of these recitations are close and all of them are correct, because they are well-known in the Arabic languages and famous in their language. And His statement,
h
What God has given me is better than what He has given you

, meaning: What God has given me of wealth and worldly life is more and better than what He has given you. Rather, you rejoice in your gift, meaning: I do not rejoice in your gift that you have given me, rather you rejoice in the gift that is given to you, because you are people who boast about the world and are proud of it, and the world and its wealth are not among my needs, because God, the Most High, has empowered me with it and given me control over it as He has given me control over it as He has given control over anyone else. Return to them, this is what Solomon said to the woman’s messenger, Return to them, and we will come to them with soldiers they cannot resist, meaning they have no power over them and no ability to prevent them from what they wanted from them.
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When the gifts came to Solomon, containing female slaves and male slave girls, purebred horses, and various worldly goods, he said to the messengers who had brought them: “Do you provide me with wealth?
h
What God has given me is better than what He has given you

. Rather, you rejoice in your gifts.” This is because I have no power over your gifts, and my opinion of them is not like yours. So return to her with what you have brought from her. We will come to them with soldiers they cannot resist.

c: Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Saleh,
m: regarding his statement, Then we will come to them with soldiers they cannot resist, he said: They will have no power over them. And His statement,
h
And We will surely expel them from it

, humiliated and disgraced, means: And We will surely expel those whom You sent from their land, humiliated and disgraced, if they do not come to Me in submission. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih:
m: h
And We will surely expel them from it
, humiliated and disgraced, or let her and her people come to me as Muslims.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this word.
Some of the reciters from Medina recited it atamdudunni with two nuns and with the yaa added.
Some of the Kufians recited it in the same way, except that they deleted the yaa from the end of it and broke the final nun.
Some of the reciters from Basra recited it with two nuns and with the yaa added when connected and deleted it when stopped.
Some of the reciters from Kufa recited it with a shaddah on the nun and with the yaa added.

x: God Almighty says: Go back to them, and We will surely come to them with soldiers they cannot resist, and We will surely expel them from it humiliated and degraded.
Scholars differed as to when Solomon said, O assembly,
h
which of you will bring me her throne

Some of them said: He said that when the hoopoe came to him with the report of the woman of Sheba, and said to him, I have come to you from Sheba with certain report, and informed him that she had a great throne. So Solomon, peace be upon him, said to him, We will see whether you are telling the truth or are you among the liars. So his test of his truthfulness or his lie was when he said to these people, Which of you will bring me this woman's throne before they come to me in submission? They said: Solomon only wrote the letter with the hoopoe to the woman after he had confirmed the truth of the hoopoe's statement that the woman had brought him her throne, as the hoopoe had described it. They said: If it were not for that, it would have been impossible for him to write a letter with him to someone who did not know whether he was still alive or not. They said: Another thing is that if he had written a letter with the hoopoe to the woman before her throne came to him, and before he knew that the hoopoe was telling the truth, then his saying to him, We will see whether you are truthful or you are among the liars, would have no meaning, because his second information about him informing her of the letter, or his leaving it out of her information, would not have been related to anything other than what he knew about his first information when he said to him, I have come to you from Sheba with certain report.

They said: Even if there was no book with them to test his truthfulness or his falsehood, and it was impossible for the Prophet of God to say something that had no meaning and he had said, We will see whether you are truthful or you are among the liars, it is known that what tested the hoopoe’s truthfulness or his falsehood was the woman’s throne coming to him, according to what the hoopoe, the witness to his truthfulness, had told him, and then the book was with him after that to her.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Solomon was given a kingdom, and he did not know that anyone else had been given a kingdom. When he lost the hoopoe, he asked him: Where did you come from? And he promised him a severe threat of killing and torment. He said: I have come to you from Sheba with certain report. Solomon said to him: What is this report? The hoopoe said: Indeed, I found a woman in Sheba ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne. When the hoopoe informed Solomon that he had found authority, he denied that anyone on earth had authority other than him, so he said to those of the jinn and humans who were with him, O eminent ones, which of you will bring me my throne before they come to me in submission? An Ifrit from the jinn said, I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed, I am for this [religious] strength and trustworthiness. Solomon said, I want something faster than that.
h
He who had knowledge of the Book said
h
I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you

. So he called upon the name while it was standing with him, and the throne bore it with patience until it was placed before Solomon, and God did that. When Solomon was brought the throne, and they were polytheists who prostrated to the sun and the moon, the hoopoe informed him of that, so he wrote a letter with it and then sent it to them. When the hoopoe came to the queen, he threw the letter to her. She said, “O eminent ones, indeed I A noble letter was thrown to me...to...and come to me in submission." So she said to her people what she said: "And indeed, I am sending to them a gift and I will see with what the messengers return." He said: And she sent to him female slaves and slave girls, and dressed them in the same garment, so that the male could not be distinguished from the female. She said: If there is separation between them until the male is distinguished from the female, then return the gift, then he is a prophet and it is appropriate for us to leave our kingdom and follow his religion and join him. So Solomon returned the gift and there was separation between them. He said: These are boys and these are slave girls. And he said: "Do you provide me with wealth while what God has given me is better than what He has given you? Rather, it is you who rejoice in your gift."...to the end of the verse.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak, who said regarding His statement, “Indeed, I found a woman ruling over them”… the verse, he said: And Solomon denied that anyone on earth had authority other than him, so he said to those around him from the jinn and mankind,
h
Which of you will bring me her throne
?… the verse.

x: Others said: Rather, the hoopoe tested Solomon’s truthfulness with the book, and he only asked the one who was with him to bring him the woman’s throne after his messengers had left him, and after the woman had come to him.

Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: When the messengers returned to her with what Solomon had said, she said: By God, I know that this is not a king, and that we cannot control him, and that we will not do anything to outnumber him. Surat al-Naml 27:38 He said, "O eminent ones,
h
which of you will bring me her throne

before they come to me in submission?" She sent word: I am coming to you with the kings of my people, so that I may see what your command is and what you will call for in your religion. Then she ordered that her royal throne, on which she used to sit, be made of gold inlaid with rubies, emeralds, and pearls, and placed in seven chambers, one inside the other. Then she locked the doors, and only women served her. She had six hundred women with her to serve her.

Then she said to those she left in charge of her sultanate: Keep what is before you and my royal throne, so that none of God’s servants may reach it, and no one may see it until I come to you. Then she went to Solomon with twelve thousand kings of Yemen, each of whom had many thousands under his command. So Solomon began to send the jinn, who would bring him her route and her destination every day and night, until when she drew near, he gathered the jinn and humans under his command, and said, O chiefs,
h
which of you will bring me her throne
before they come to me in submission? The interpretation of the words: Solomon said to the nobles of his army of jinn and humans who were present with him, O assembly,
h
which of you will bring me her throne
? meaning her bed.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Which of you will bring me her throne
? He said: A bed on a couch.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Her throne is a bed on a couch. Ibn Jurayj said: A bed of gold, its legs of jewels and pearls.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some scholars, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih:
m: h
Which of you will bring me her throne
?: her bed. Ibn Zayd said about this:

c: Ibn Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement,

? He said: Her seat. Scholars differed about the reason why Solomon asked the leaders of his army to bring this woman’s throne from among her possessions before her conversion to Islam.

x: Some of them said: He did that because he was pleased when the hoopoe described its features to him, and he feared that she would convert to Islam and her property would be forbidden to him, so he wanted to take her throne before it was forbidden to him to take it with her conversion to Islam.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Solomon told the hoopoe that she had come out to come to him, and he was told about her throne, and he was amazed. It was made of gold and its legs were made of jewels crowned with pearls. He knew that if they came to him as Muslims, their wealth would not be permissible for them, so he said to the jinn,
h
Which of you will bring me her throne
h
before they come to me as Muslims

x: Others said: Rather, Solomon did that to rebuke her and test her intelligence, whether she would confirm it when she saw it or deny it.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: God informed Solomon that it was coming, so he said:
h
Which of you will bring me her throne
before they come to me in submission so that he could reproach her, and the kings would reproach one another based on knowledge. The commentators differed in their interpretation of his statement,
h
Before they come to me as Muslims

x: Some of them said: It means before they come to me as willing submitters.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, before they come to me in submission, meaning: obedient.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is:
h
Before they come to me as Muslims
, who accept Islam, which is the religion of God.
Those who said this were mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said:
m: Ibn Jurayj said,
h
Which of you will bring me her throne
h
before they come to me as Muslims
? with the sanctity of Islam, he will prevent them and their money, meaning Islam will prevent them.

x: The most correct of the statements about the reason why Solomon singled out the leaders of his army to bring him the offering of this woman, without the rest of her kingdom, according to us, so that he might make that a proof against her of his prophethood, and so that she might know by that the power of God and the greatness of His status, is that she left him in a house within houses, some within others, closed and locked upon her. So God brought him out of all of that, without opening the locks or doors, until He brought him to His guardian from among His creation, and delivered him to him. So that was for her the greatest proof of the truth of what Solomon had called her to, and of the truth of Solomon in what he informed her of regarding his prophethood. As for the interpretation that is more appropriate for his statement,
h
Before they come to me as Muslims

, it is the statement of Ibn Abbas that we mentioned before, that its meaning is obedient, because the woman did not come to Solomon when she came to him as a Muslim, but rather she became a Muslim after her arrival to him and after a dialogue and questioning took place between them.

And His statement, An Ifrit from among the jinn said, God Almighty says: A chief from among the jinn, a mighty ogre, said. The Arabs have two dialects for this: Ifrit and Ifriya. So whoever says Ifriya, their plural is Affari, and whoever says Ifrit, their plural is Afareet. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said, An Ifrit from the jinn said, he said: a rebel from the jinn, I will bring it to you before you rise from your place.

m: and others, similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of some of his companions,

m: A genie said, whose name is Kuzan. His saying:

means: I will bring you her throne before you rise from this seat of yours. It was mentioned that he was sitting to judge between people, so he said: I will bring it to you before you rise from this seat in which you sat to judge between people. It was mentioned that he used to sit until midday. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. He said: Al-Husayn told us, he said:

m: similarly. He said: And he was judging. He said: Before you get up from the place where you are judging.

m: h

, meaning his assembly. And his saying: And indeed, I am strong and trustworthy over it despite the jewels in it, and I will not betray it. It has been said: He is trustworthy with regard to women’s vaginas.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, And indeed, I am strong and trustworthy over it, he said: Strong to bear it, trustworthy with regard to this woman’s relief. His saying,
h
He who had knowledge of the Book said
, God Almighty says: He who had knowledge of the Book of God said, and he was a man, as mentioned, from the sons of Adam.

x: Some of them said: His name was Balikha.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abu Uthma told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Bishr, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement, He who had knowledge of the Scripture said, he said: His name was Balikha.

c: Yahya bin Dawud Al-Wasiti told us: Abu Usama told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh,
m: regarding his statement, who has knowledge of the Book, meaning a human being.

c: Ibn Arafa told us: Marwan bin Muawiyah Al-Fazari told us, on the authority of Al-Ala bin Eid Al-Karim, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, He who had knowledge from the Scripture said, ‘I will bring it to you.’ He said: I will look into the Book of my Lord, then
h
I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you
. He said: So that scholar spoke words that entered the Throne under the Throne under the earth until he came out to them.

c: Ibn Arafa told us: Hammad bin Muhammad told me, on the authority of Uthman bin Matar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said:
m: The one who had knowledge of the Book called out: O our God and the God of all things, one God, there is no god but You, bring me her throne. He said: So it appeared before him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us,
m: Abu Sufyan said, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
h
He who had knowledge of the Book said
, he said: A man from the children of Adam, I think he said from the children of Israel, who knew the name of God by which if He is called upon, He answers.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, who has knowledge of the Book, he said: The name by which if He is called upon, He answers, and it is: O Possessor of Majesty and Honor.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: Solomon said to those around him,
h
Which of you will bring me her throne

before they come to me in submission? An Ifrit said, I will bring it to you before you rise from your place. Solomon said, I want something faster than that. A man from among the people who had knowledge of the Book said, meaning the name of God by which if He is called upon, He answers. Surat al-Naml 27:38 He said, "O eminent ones,
h
which of you will bring me her throne
before they come to me in submission?"

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: “An ‘Ifrit from among the jinn said: ‘I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed, I am for this [religious] strong and trustworthy.’ I will not bring you anything else. I will say something else, and I will give you an example of it.” He said: On that day, a worshipper went out to an island in the sea, and when he heard the ‘Ifrit, he said: ‘I will bring it to you before you blink again.’ He said: Then he called upon one of the names of God, and behold, it was being carried between his eyes, and he recited: ‘And when he saw it settled before him, he said: This is from the bounty of my Lord…’ until he reached: ‘Indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous.’”

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: A human being said. He said: And Mujahid said: The one who has knowledge of the Book: knowledge of the name of God.

x: Others said: The one who had knowledge of the Book was Asif.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: “An Ifrit said to Solomon: ‘I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed, I am for this [the truth] strong and trustworthy.’” They claimed that Solomon, son of David, said: I seek something more urgent than this. Asaf, son of Yarkhya, who was a truthful person and knew the greatest name by which if God is called upon, He answers, and if He is asked by it, He gives, said: I, O Prophet of God, will bring it to you before you blink. His saying,
h
I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you

x: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that.
Some of them said that its meaning is: I will bring it to you before anyone of you who is within sight of you reaches you.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ibrahim told us, he said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: h
Before your glance returns to you
, he said: Before the furthest thing you see
h
returns to you
, so that is what His statement,
h
Before your glance returns to you
. He said: Al-Hussein told us, he said:

m: He said: Other than Qatada said,
h
Before your glance returns to you
before a person comes to you from the distance of the eye.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: before your eyes reach their limit and end.

m: h
Before your glance returns to you
means you stretch your eyes, but your glance does not reach its limit until I present it before you. He said: That is what I mean.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Othman told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: I was told that he said: Raise your gaze from where he is coming from. But he did not look back at him until the Throne was placed before him.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Before your glance returns to you
, he said: He extended his sight.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
Before your glance returns to you
, he said: When he stretches his gaze until the glance cools down, defeated.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
Before your glance returns to you
, he said: When he extends his sight until his glance is uncovered.

x: The more correct of the two opinions is the one that says:
h
Before your glance returns to you
from its furthest point. This is because the meaning of His statement,
h
Returns to you
, is that sight
h
returns to you

when you open the eye, not returning, but rather extends forward until the point where its light extends reaches its end. So if that is the case, and God only informed us about the one who said that, I will bring it to you before it returns, then it is not for us to say,
h
I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you
from its point of end. His saying,

And when he saw it settled near him

, means: When Solomon saw the throne of the Queen of Sheba settled near him. There is something omitted in the speech that is sufficient in terms of the evidence of what was apparent in what was omitted, which is: So he called upon God, and it was brought to him. When Solomon saw it settled near him.
He mentioned that the scholar called upon God. The throne opened in the place where it had been, and then a spring sprang forth from under the ground before Solomon.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said:
m: They mentioned that Asif ibn Barkhiya performed ablution, then bowed two rak’ahs, then said: O Prophet of God, extend your eyes until your blink ends. So Solomon extended his eyes looking at him towards Yemen, and Asif called out, and the throne was torn apart in the place where it was, then it sprang up before Solomon. “And when Solomon saw it settled near him, he said: This is from the bounty of my Lord to test me.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Her throne sprang from under the earth. And his saying, He said, ‘This is from the bounty of my Lord, that He may test me,’ meaning: This sight, power, kingdom, and authority that I have, until this provision was conveyed to me in the amount of time it takes for an eye to move from Ma’rib to Ash-Sham, is from the bounty of my Lord, which He has favored over me and the gift that He has bestowed upon me, that He may test me, meaning: to test me and examine me, should I be grateful for what He has done for me, or should I be ungrateful for His favor upon me by not being grateful to Him. It has been said that its meaning is: Should I be grateful for this woman’s honor when she brought it, or should I be ungrateful when I saw someone who is less knowledgeable than me in this world?

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata’ al-Khurasani told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement, “
h
And when he saw it settled near him

, he said, ‘This is from the bounty of my Lord to test me whether I will be grateful’ for the throne when it was brought to me ‘or disbelieve’ when I see someone who is lower than me in this world who is more knowledgeable than me?’” And His statement, And whoever is grateful is only grateful for himself, meaning: And whoever is grateful for God’s blessing and favor upon him, is only grateful to seek benefit for himself, because he does not benefit anyone other than himself by that, because God has no need of any of His creation. Rather, He called them to thank Him as an exposure from Him to them for benefit, not to bring benefit to Him through their thanking Him, nor to ward off harm from Him. And whoever is ungrateful, then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous, meaning: And whoever is ungrateful for His blessings, His kindness to him, and His favor upon him, then he has wronged himself and his portion will be diminished, and God is Free of need of His gratitude, He has no need of it, and the ingratitude of those of His creation who are ungrateful to Him does not harm Him. He is Generous, and from His generosity is His favors upon those who are ungrateful for His blessings, and make them a connection by which they reach His disobedience.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: An Ifrit from among the jinn said, ‘I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed, I am for this strong and trustworthy.’
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “He who had knowledge of the Scripture said, ‘I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.’

m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement,

, he said: Her seat in which she sits.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say, regarding His statement,
h
They denied her throne
, he commanded them to add to it and subtract from it. And his saying,
h
We will see whether she will be guided

, meaning: We will see whether she will understand and confirm that her throne is hers. Or will she be among those who are not guided? meaning: among those who do not understand and thus will not confirm her throne. It was said that Solomon denied her throne and ordered that a palace be built for her because the devils had told him that she had no mind and that her legs were like a donkey’s hoof. So he wanted to know the truth of what he had been told about that. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement,
h
Will you be guided or will you be among those who are not guided
? the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: We will see whether you are guided or whether you are among those who are not guided. He said: Her throne was increased and decreased in order to see her mind, and she was found to be of sound mind.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: We will see if you are guided means if you recognize him.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Let us see if you will be guided
, he said: you will recognize it.

c: Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih:
m: Will you be guided, or will you be among those who are not guided? That is, will you understand, or will you be among those who do not understand. So he did that to see whether he would recognize him or not.

x: God Almighty says: When the lady of Sheba came to Solomon, he brought out her throne for her. He said to her: Is this your throne? She said, likening it to him: It is as if it were the same. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said:
m: When she went to Solomon and spoke to him, he brought out her throne for her, then said: Is this your throne? She said: It is as if it is.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “So when she came, it was said: ‘Is this your throne?’ She said: ‘It is as if it were the same.’” He said: She resembled it, and she had left it behind her.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: My father used to tell us this entire hadith, meaning the hadith of Solomon, and this woman, and when she came, “It was said: Is this your throne?” She said: It is as if it is the same. She complained. And His statement:
h
And we were given knowledge before her
, God Almighty says, informing us of what Solomon said, and Solomon said:
h
And we were given knowledge before her
, meaning this woman, by God and His ability to do whatever He wills, and we were Muslims to God before her. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And we were given knowledge before it, it was said: Solomon said it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: God Almighty says: And He prevented this woman, the owner of Sheba, from worshipping God, what she used to worship besides God, and that was her worship of the sun. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And what she used to worship besides God turned her away, he said: Her disbelief in God’s decree, other than the idol, that she be guided to the truth.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And what she used to worship besides God prevented her from being guided to the truth. He said: Her disbelief in God’s decree prevented her from being guided to the truth.

x: If it were said: The meaning of that is: And what she used to worship besides God prevented her from being guided to the truth, meaning: He prevented her and stood between her and him, that would be a good interpretation. If it were also said: And God prevented her from that by guiding her to Islam, that would also be a correct interpretation. His statement: Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people means: This woman was a disbeliever from a disbelieving people. The lāf in his statement indeed is broken as a subject. Whoever interprets his statement: And what she used to worship besides God in the same way we have, then ma in his statement: what she used to worship is in the nominative case due to becoming prevented, because the meaning is that what prevented her from worshipping God was not her ignorance or that she did not understand, rather what prevented her from worshipping God was her worship of the sun and the moon, and that was from the religion of her people and her fathers, so she followed in their footsteps.
Whoever interprets it in the other two ways, then ma is in the accusative case.

It is mentioned that when the mistress of Sheba came to Solomon, he ordered the devils to build him a tower, which was like a roof made of glass, and he made water run underneath it to test her mind and understanding in the same way that she used to direct the female and male servants to him to distinguish between the males and females among them, as a reprimand for that as well. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Solomon ordered the palace to be built, and the devils had made it for him from glass, the whiteness of which was like water. Then water was sent beneath it, and his bed was placed in it, and he sat on it, and the birds, jinn, and humans were devoted to it. Then he said: Enter the palace, to show her a kingdom more honorable than her kingdom, and a power greater than her power.
h
When she saw it
, she thought it was a sea and uncovered her legs, not doubting that it was water she was wading through. It was said to her: Enter, for
h
it is a palace smooth of glass

. When she stood before Solomon, he called her to worship God and rebuked her for worshipping the sun instead of God. She said what the heretics said, and Solomon fell down in prostration in awe of what she said, and the people prostrated with him, and she fell at her hands when she saw Solomon do what he did. When Solomon raised his head, he said: Woe to you, what did you say? He said: And I forgot what she said. So she said: My Lord, I have wronged myself and I have submitted. With Solomon, to God, Lord of the worlds.” And she converted to Islam, and her conversion was good. It was said that Solomon ordered the construction of the palace as God had described it, because the jinn feared that Solomon would marry her, so they wanted to make him lose interest in her, so they said: Her husband is a donkey, and her mother was a jinn.

c: So Solomon wanted to know the truth of what the jinn had told him
m: about that. Mention who said that. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Maʿshar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi, who said: The jinn said to Solomon, making him renounce Bilqis, Her husband is the husband of a donkey, and her mother was a jinn. So Solomon ordered the palace to be built, and in it were imprisoned sea creatures: whales and frogs. When she saw the palace, she said: The son of David has not found a punishment that could kill me except drowning? “
h
I thought it was a sea

,” and she uncovered her shins. He said: So when people felt her legs and feet, he said: So Solomon was reluctant to spare her shins from the razor. K said: So the lime was made for that reason. I believe it is possible that Solomon ordered the construction of the palace for the two reasons mentioned by Wahb and Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, to test her intelligence and look at her leg and foot, to know the truth of what was said to him about her. Mujahid used to say, as mentioned about the meaning of the palace, what:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, the palace, he said: A pool of water upon which Solomon made vessels which he dressed. He said: And Bilqis was a tall, poetic woman, her foot like a donkey’s hoof, and her mother was a jinn.

c: Ahmad bin Al-Waleed Al-Ramli told me: Hisham bin Ammar told us: Al-Waleed bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Bashir, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Anas, on the authority of Bashir bin Nahik, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘One of the parents of the woman of Saba’ was a jinn.’” He said: Safwan bin Saleh told us, he said:

c: Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Bashir, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Bashir bin Nahik, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, that Al-Nadr bin Anas was mentioned. His saying:
h
When she saw it

, she thought it was a sea. He says: When the woman saw the tower, she thought it was a sea because of its whiteness and the turbulence of the sea creatures beneath it, and she uncovered her legs to wade through it to Solomon. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: She was told to enter the palace, and
h
when she saw it
, she thought it was a sea. He said: It was made of glass, and the water was behind it, so she thought it was a sea. He said: Al-Hussein told us, he said:

c: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: his statement:
h
I thought it was a sea
, he said: a sea.

c: Amr ibn Ali told us: Ibn Suwar told us: Ruh ibn al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: And she uncovered her legs, and behold, they were hairy. So he said: Is there nothing that will remove this? They said: The razor. He said: No, the razor leaves a mark. So he ordered that a depilatory cream be used, and it was done.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Hafs told us, on the authority of Imran bin Sulayman, on the authority of Ikrimah and Abu Salih, who said:
m: When Sulayman married Bilqis, she said to him: No iron has ever touched me. Sulayman said to the devils: Look at what removes hair. They said: Lime. So he was the first to make Lime. And His saying:
h
It is a palace smooth of glass
, God Almighty says: Solomon said to her: This is not a sea,
h
it is a palace smooth of glass
. He says: It is only a building constructed and erected from glass. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Murad he said:
m: built. And His statement: She said, ‘My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon…’… the verse, God Almighty says: The woman of Sheba said: My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself in my worship of the sun and my prostration to those other than You, and I submit with Solomon to God. She says: And I submitted with Solomon, submitting to God in monotheism, singling out for Him divinity and lordship without anyone else. Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: in
h
I thought it was a sea
h
It is a palace smooth of glass
. Then she knew that she had been defeated. “She said: My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds.”

x: God Almighty says: “And We had certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih, [saying], ‘Worship God’ alone, with no partner, and do not make any god with Him. Then at once they were two disputing parties.” He says: So when Salih came to them, calling them to God, his people from Thamud became two disputing parties regarding what he called them to. One party believed in Salih and had faith in him, and another party denied him and disbelieved in what he brought. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, concerning the statement of God, Two parties are disputing, he said: A believer and a disbeliever. Their statement righteous is a mursal, and their statement righteous is not a mursal. And what is meant by His statement, are disputing is that they differ.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then they will be two parties disputing. He said: A believer and a disbeliever. And His statement: He said, ‘O my people,
h
why do you hasten the evil before the good
?’ God Almighty says: Salih said to his al-Nas 114:O my people, why do you hasten the punishment of God before the mercy?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
Why do you hasten the evil before the good
? He said: The evil is the punishment, before the good is before mercy.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He said, ‘O my people, why do you hasten the evil?’ He said, The punishment before the good. He said, The well-being. His statement: Why do you not ask forgiveness of God that you may receive mercy? means: Why do you not repent to God for your disbelief, so that your Lord may forgive you for your great crime and pardon you for His punishment of you for the great sin you have committed? And His saying: Perhaps you will receive mercy means: So that your Lord may have mercy on you by asking Him for forgiveness for your disbelief.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘O my people, why do you hasten the evil before the good?
Why do you not ask forgiveness of God that you may receive mercy?’

God Almighty says: Thamud said to their messenger Salih, We consider you and those with you to be an ill omen. That is, we considered you and those with you to be our followers, and we drove away the birds, telling them that hardships and calamities would befall us because of you and them. Salih answered them and said, Your bad omen is with God. That is, what you drove away from the birds because of the hardships that would befall you is known to God. He does not know which of them will happen, or what you think of the calamities or hardships, or what you hope for of well-being, hope, and love. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: “He said: Your omen is with God” means: your misfortunes.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
Your omen is with God means your knowledge is with God

. And His statement: Rather, you are a people who are being tested, meaning: Rather, you are a people who are being tested. Your Lord tests you when He sent me to you. Will you obey Him and do what He commands you to do, so He will reward you abundantly with His reward? Or will you disobey Him and do the opposite of what He commands, so His punishment will befall you?

x: God the Most High says: “And in the city of Salih, which was the city of Thamud, there were nine people who were spreading corruption on the earth and were not doing good. Their corruption on the earth was their disbelief in God and their disobedience to Him. God the Most High singled out these nine people with the report that they were spreading corruption on the earth and were not doing good, even though all the disbelievers were corrupters on the earth. This is because these nine are the ones who, as we have heard, strove to hamstring the she-camel, and cooperated in this and formed an alliance to kill Salih from among the people of Thamud. We have already mentioned their stories and accounts in the previous part of this book of ours. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, “Nine men,” he said: From the people of Salih.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And there were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform they were those who hamstrung the she-camel

, and when they hamstrung it they said: We will let Salih and his family spend the night and kill them, then we will say to the friends of Salih: We did not witness any of this, and we have no knowledge of it. So God destroyed them all. And His statement: They said, ‘Swear by God that we will surely kill him and his family by night.’ God Almighty says: These nine men who spread corruption in the land of Thamud and did not reform said, “Swear by God, O people, let some of you swear to others: ‘We will surely kill Salih and his family by night, then we will kill him, then we will say to his guardian: We did not witness the destruction of his family.’” And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, They swore by God: He said: They swore an oath to destroy him, but they did not reach him until they and all their people were destroyed.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar. His statement, They swore by God has two meanings: One of them is the accusative case as a predicate, as if it were said: They said, dividing. It has been mentioned that this is in the reading of Abdullah, and it is not appropriate to divide by God, and it does not have the word said in it, so that of his readings indicates the accusative case in they divided as I have described. The other meaning is the jussive, as if some of them said to each other: They swore by God. According to this second meaning, the reading of we will spend the night with the ya' and the nun is appropriate, because the one who said to them divided, and even if he is the one who gives the order, then it is for the one who swore, as is said in speech, Get up, let us go to so-and-so or Get up, let us go to him. According to the first meaning, which is the accusative case, reading it with the nun is more eloquent, because its meaning is: They said, dividing, we will spend the night. The ya' is also permissible in this way, as is said in speech, They said, let us honor your father and Let us honor your father." The readers of Medina, the majority of the readers of Basra, and some of the Kufians read this with the nun. The most common reading among the people of Kufa is to read it with the letter Ya and the letter Ta with the Damma. However, some of the people of Mecca read it with the letter Ya. The most amazing reading in this regard is with the letter nun, because that is the most eloquent speech in the two ways that I explained of the accusative and the jussive, even though all of that is correct and not corrupted for what I described. The most hated reading with it is with the letter ya because few people read it like that. And his saying We will spend the night with him, he said: They will spend the night with Salih and then kill him. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated from Ibn Ishaq: He said: The nine who hamstrung the she-camel said: Come, let us kill Salih. If he is truthful, meaning in what he promised them of punishment after the three days, we will hasten it before him, and if he is lying, we will have caught up with his she-camel. So they came to him at night to spend the night with his family, but the angels struck them with stones. When they were slow to reach their companions, they came to Salih’s house and found them beaten with stones. And His statement: And indeed, we are truthful means you say to his guardian: And indeed, we are truthful. We did not witness the destruction of his family.
