According to this second meaning, the reading of we will spend the night with the ya' and the nun is appropriate, because the one who said to them divided, and even if he is the one who gives the order, then it is for the one who swore, as is said in speech, Get up, let us go to so-and-so or Get up, let us go to him.
The readers of Medina, the majority of the readers of Basra, and some of the Kufians read this with the nun.
The most common reading among the people of Kufa is to read it with the letter Ya and the letter Ta with the Damma.
However, some of the people of Mecca read it with the letter Ya.
The most hated reading with it is with the letter ya because few people read it like that.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “They said, ‘We swear by God that we will surely kill him and his family by night, then we will surely say to his guardian, “We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed, we are truthful.”’”

God Almighty says: And these nine men who spread corruption on earth betrayed Salih by going to him at night to kill him and his family, and Salih was unaware of that. And We planned a plan, meaning: So We seized them with Our punishment, and hastened the punishment for them, while they did not perceive of Our plan. We have previously explained the meaning of God’s deception of those against whom He deceived, and the reason for that, and that He took those among them by surprise or led those among them to disbelieve in Him and disobey Him, then brought down the punishment upon them by surprise and negligence. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shammar bin Atiyah, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ali, he said:
m: Deceit is treachery, treachery is disbelief.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And they plotted a plot

, and We plotted a plot, he said: They plotted for their affair, and God plotted for them, and they plotted against Salih a plot, and We plotted against them a plot, while they did not perceive our plot, and We perceived their plot. They said: Salih claimed that he would finish with us in three days, but we would finish with him and his family before that. He had a mosque in the Hijr in a valley where he prayed, so they went out to the cave and said: When he comes to pray, we will kill him, then we will return when we have finished with him to his family, so we left them. And he recited the words of God Almighty: “They said, ‘We swear by God that we will surely kill him and his family by night, and then we will surely say to his friend, “We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed, we are truthful.”’” So God sent a rock from the plateau in front of them, and they feared that it would crush them, so they rushed to the cave, and the rock closed over them at the mouth of the cave, and their people did not know where they were, nor did they know what had happened to their people. So God Almighty punished these here, and those there, and God saved Salih and those with him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan. He said: So God sent a rock upon them and killed them. And His statement: Then see how was the end of their plot, God Almighty says: So look, O Muhammad, with one eye at the end of the treachery of Thamud against Salih, how it was, and what their aggression and denial brought about, for that is our way with those who deny Our messengers and transgress against us from among all creation. So beware your people from Quraysh, lest they be afflicted by their denial of you with what Thamud afflicted by their denial of Salih from the three tribes. His saying: We destroyed them and their people, all together. He says: We destroyed the nine men who were spreading corruption on earth from the people of Salih and their people from Thamud, all together, and We did not leave a single one of them. The reciters differed in reading his statement: Indeed, We so the majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Basra read it with a kasra as an introductory letter, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa read it Ana dammarnahum with a fatha on the alif. If it is a fatha, then there are two ways of iqrab in Ana: one of them is the nominative case in reference to the consequence in following it, and the other is the accusative case in reference to the position of how, because it is in the accusative case if you like, and if you like, in repetition of was on it in the manner: So see how was the consequence of their plot, the consequence of their plot was Our destruction of them.

x: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions, and they are close in meaning, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in reading his statement: Indeed, We so the majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Basra read it with a kasra as an introductory letter, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa read it Ana dammarnahum with a fatha on the alif.

Abu Jaafar said: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions, and they are close in meaning, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “Then see how was the outcome of their plot.
We destroyed them and their people, all together.”

The Most High means by His statement: Those are their houses, empty, those are their dwellings, empty of them, with none of them in them. God destroyed them and annihilated them. Because of their wrongdoing, God Almighty says: Because of their wronging themselves, by associating partners with God, and denying their Messenger. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who know, God Almighty says: Indeed, in Our action with Thamud, what We related to you, O Muhammad, of the story, is a lesson for those who know what We did to them, from your people who deny what you brought them from your Lord, and a warning. And We saved those who believed, He says: And We saved from Our vengeance and punishment which We brought upon Thamud, Our Messenger Salih, and the believers in him. And they were fearing God, He says: And they were fearing God by their faith and by their belief in Salih, who brought upon their people from Thamud what befell them of God’s punishment. Thus, We will save you, O Muhammad, and your followers, when We bring upon the polytheists of Your people are among them. It was mentioned that when God made what he made permissible for his people, Salih and the believers in him went out to the Levant, and settled in Ramlat, Palestine.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And We saved those who believed and were fearing God.

God the Almighty says: And We sent Lot to his people, when he said to them: O my people, Do you commit immorality while you see? That it is immoral, because you know that no one had done what you did before. And His statement: Do you indeed approach men out of desire? is from you in that, instead of the vaginas of women, which God has permitted you through marriage. And His statement: Rather, you are a people behaving ignorantly. He says: This is not from you except that you are a foolish people, ignorant of the great right of God upon you, so you disobeyed His command and disobeyed His Messenger.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Do you indeed approach men with desire instead of women?
Rather, you are a people behaving ignorantly.

God Almighty says: The people of Lot had no answer to him, when he forbade them from what God had commanded them to do, which was to have intercourse with men, except that some of them said to one another, “Expel the family of Lot from your city. Indeed, they are
h
people who purify themselves
” from what we do, which is having intercourse with men in their backsides.

c: As Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said:
m: I heard Al-Hasan bin Amara mentioning on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement,
h
People who purify themselves
, he said: from men and women having intercourse in their backsides.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, they are
h
people who purify themselves
, he said: from the backsides of men and the backsides of women, mocking them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: They purify themselves from the backsides of men and women, they say that in mockery of them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: that he recited, Indeed, they are
h
people who purify themselves
. He said: They criticised them without fault: meaning, they purify themselves from evil deeds.

x: God Almighty says: So We saved Lot and his family, except for his wife, from Our punishment when We made it a trial for them. Then We destined her meaning that We destined his wife: We made her, by Our decree, among those who remained behind among those who remained.

And We rained down upon them a rain meaning that God rained down upon them from the sky stones of baked clay. How evil was the rain of those who were warned. He says: So evil was that rain, the rain of the people whom God warned of His punishment for their disobedience to Him, and frightened them with His wrath by sending the Messenger to them with that.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say, O Muhammad, ‘Praise be to God,’ for His blessings upon us, and for granting us success in what He has granted us of guidance. ‘And peace,’ meaning: and security from Him from His punishment with which He punished the people of Lot and the people of Salih, upon those whom He chose, meaning: those whom He chose for His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and made them his companions and ministers in the religion to which He sent him, calling to it, rather than those who associate others with Him and deny the prophethood of His Prophet. And in a similar manner to what we said in interpreting that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Talq told us,
m: meaning Ibn Ghannam, on the authority of Ibn Zuhair, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “And peace be upon His chosen servants.” He said: The companions of Muhammad, whom God chose for His Prophet.

c: Ali bin Sahl told us: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us:
m: I said to Abdullah bin Mubarak: Tell me about the statement of God, “Say, ‘Praise be to God, and peace be upon His chosen servants.’” Who are these? He told me on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, who said: They are the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement,
h
Is God better or do they associate others with Him

? God the Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to those of your people whose deeds We have made pleasing to them, while they are wandering blindly: Is God, who has bestowed these blessings upon His allies, which He has related to you in this Surah, and destroyed His enemies with the kinds of punishment He has mentioned to you, good? Do you not associate others with Him from your idols that neither benefit you nor harm you, nor ward off harm from themselves or their allies, nor bring any benefit to themselves or to them? God the Almighty says: This matter is not difficult for one who has reason, so how can you permit yourself to associate the worship of One who can neither benefit you nor ward off harm from you, with the worship of One in whose hand is benefit and harm, and to whom belongs everything? Then God the Almighty began to enumerate His blessings upon them and His favors toward them, and to inform them of their lack of gratitude to Him for what He has bestowed upon them, so He says, Is He who created the heavens and the earth?

x: God the Almighty says to the polytheists of Quraysh 106:Is the worship of your idols that can neither harm nor benefit better, or the worship of Him who created the heavens and the earth? And He sent down for you water from the sky meaning rain. It may also be possible that He meant the springs that He caused to gush forth in the earth, because all of that is from His creation. Then We caused to grow thereby meaning with the water that He sent down from the sky gardens which is the plural of garden. A garden is an orchard with a wall surrounding it. If there is no wall around it, it is not a garden. His statement of delight means: of a beautiful view. It has also been said that it means of beauty in the sense of monotheism, and it has also been said that it means gardens, just as He said: And to God belong the best names, and I have explained that previously. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement,
h
Gardens of delight
, he said: Delight is the fruit of what people and livestock eat.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Gardens of delight
, he said: of everything that people and livestock eat. And His statement,
h
It was not for you to cause its trees to grow

, meaning, the Most High says: We caused these gardens to grow with the water We sent down from the sky for you. For you would not have been able, had He not sent down water from the sky, to cause the trees of these gardens to grow, and you would not have been able to do that, because that is not possible except with water. And His statement,
h
Is there a god with God
? means, the Most High says: Is there a worshipped god with God, O ignorant ones, who created that and sent down water from the sky, thereby causing gardens to grow for you? So His statement,
h
Is there a god
? is rejected by the interpretation:
h
Is there a god with God

? Rather, they are a people who ascribe equals, meaning, the Most High says: Rather, these polytheists are a people of misguidance, who deviate from the truth and transgress against it, deliberately, despite their knowledge that they are in error and misguidance. They did not deviate out of ignorance, that the One who is not able to benefit or harm is better than he who created the heavens and the earth and performed these actions. But they acted according to their knowledge and understanding, following the example of their forefathers who came before them.

x: God the Most High says: “Is the worship of that which you associate with your Lord better, O people, while it neither harms nor benefits, or He who has made the earth for you a resting place upon which you settle, not that it moves with you? And He has made rivers for you in its midst, meaning: rivers between them. And He has placed for it firm mountains, and placed a barrier between the two seas, between the fresh and the salty, lest one of them spoil the other. Is there a god with God other than Him who has done these things, so you have associated Him in your worship of Him? And His statement, “
h
But most of them do not know

,” Allāh the Most High says: Rather, most of these polytheists do not know the extent of God’s greatness, nor the harm that comes to them in associating others with Him in the worship of God, nor the benefit that comes to them in singling out God as divinity, devoting worship to Him alone, and disavowing every deity other than Him.
God Almighty says: Or is what you associate with God better, or He who answers the distressed one when he calls upon Him and removes the evil that befalls him?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement, And removes evil, he said: harm. His statement, and makes you successors on the earth, means: And after your rulers on the earth, He will appoint living successors from among you to succeed them. His statement,
h
Is there a god with God
? means:
h
Is there a god with God

other than Him who does these things to you and bestows these blessings upon you? His statement, How little do you remember? means: Remembering little of God’s greatness and favors to you, you remember and consider God’s proofs against you as being easy. That is why you associated others with God in your worship.

x: God Almighty says: Or is what you associate with God better? Or is He who guides you in the darknesses of the land and sea when you stray therein, and the paths therein are darkened to you?

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hussein narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Who guides you through the darknesses of the land and the sea
? The darkness on the land means the path of error, and the sea means its path and direction and what is in it. His statement,
h
And He who sends the winds as broadcasting before His mercy
, means: And He who sends the winds as broadcasting of the deadness of the earth before His mercy, meaning: before the rain that revives the deadness of the earth. And His statement,
h
Is there a deity with God
? Exalted is God above what they associate with Him? God Almighty says:
h
Is there a deity with God

other than God who would do any of that to you, so that you would worship Him instead of Him, or associate Him in your worship of Him? Exalted is God, means: To God belong the highest and most exalted position, above your association with Him, and your worship of what you worship with Him.

x: God Almighty says: Or is that which you associate with Him better, O people? Or is He who begins creation and then repeats it, creating it from nothing, inventing it then annihilating it when He wills, then repeating it when He wills in the same form in which He existed before annihilating it? And He who provides for you from the heaven and the earth, and sends down from this rain and causes to grow from this vegetation for your sustenance and the sustenance of your livestock? Is there a god with God other than God who does that? And if they claim that a god other than God does that or part of it, then say to them, O Muhammad, Bring your proof: that is, your argument that something other than God does that, if you should be truthful in your claim. And from in amn and ma is the subject of His statement: Do they not associate with Him? And the verses after it until His statement:
h
And who provides for you from the heaven and the earth means who
, not in the sense of a question, because a question does not enter into a question.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say, O Muhammad, to those who ask you among the polytheists about the Hour, No one in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen, the knowledge of which God has kept to Himself, and from which His creation has concealed other than the Hour. Nor do they perceive, He says: No one in the heavens or the earth among His creation knows when they will be resurrected from their graves for the Hour to come.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, he said: Aisha said:
m: Whoever claims that he can tell people what will happen tomorrow has greatly slandered God, and God says: None in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen except God. The Arabists differed about the reason for raising God.

x: Some of the Basrans said: It is as you say, except for a few of them. In the wording of Ibn Masoud: A few is a substitute for the first, because you negated it from it and made it for the last.

Some of the Kufians said: If you want to imagine in min the unknown, then it is conjoined with: Say, no one knows the unseen except God. He said: It is possible for min to be definite, and what comes after except comes down to it, so it is a conjunction and not a substitute, because the first is negated and the second is affirmative, so it is in the sequence as you say: Zaid stood up except for Amr, so the second is a conjunction to the first, and the interpretation is a denial, and the report cannot be a denial, or the denial a report. He said:
And likewise in ma ya’altuhu They did it except a few
and a few, from the accusative, then it is on the exception in your worship of Him, and from the nominative, then it is on the conjunction, and it is not a substitute.

And his saying, Rather, their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter. The reciters differed in their recitation of that, so the majority of the reciters of the people of Medina, except for Abu Jaʿfar and the majority of the reciters of the people of Kufa, recited it as Rather, overtaken with a kasra on the lam of bal and a shaddah on the dal of adarak, meaning: Rather, their knowledge will overtake them, meaning their knowledge of the Hereafter will continue, whether it will happen or not. Then the ta's was assimilated into the dal, as was said: You are burdened to the earth (al-Tawbah 9:38). We have explained that previously, and it is sufficient to repeat it. The majority of the Meccan reciters read itباله دريكاهم في الِخيرهwith a sukoon on the dal and a fatha on the alif, meaning, has their knowledge overtaken the knowledge of the Hereafter? Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ used to object to what was mentioned about him in the reading of those who readباله دريكاand he used to say: Bal is an affirmation and the question in this case is a denial.

The meaning of the statement is: If it was read like thisباله دريكاthen it would not have been that their knowledge was not overtaken in the Hereafter. Ibn Muhaysin read it with the question in the way that I mentioned that Abu Amr objected to. In a similar manner to what I mentioned about the Meccans reading it, it was mentioned about Mujahid that he read it, except that he read in place of bal: umm.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abdullah bin Musa told us: Uthman bin Al-Aswad told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: that he read Or has their knowledge reached them and Ibn Abbas, according to what was reported from him, used to read by adding the ya’ in bal, then he would begin idrak by opening its alif in the form of a question and doubling the dal.

c: Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hamza,
m: saying: I heard Ibn Abbas recite: Yes, their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter, meaning that it was not overtaken. It seems that Ibn Abbas interpreted that to mean that it was meant to mock those who denied the Resurrection. The correct readings in our view are the two readings, one of which was mentioned from the reading of the people of Mecca and Basra, which is (bala adarak ʿilmihum) with a sukoon on the lam of bal and a fatha on the alif of adarak and a soft dal, and the other from the reading of Kufa, which is (bala idrak) with a kasra on the lam and a doubled dal from idrak, because these are the two readings known among the readers of the regions, so whichever one the reader recites is correct in our view. As for the reading mentioned from Ibn Abbas, even if it is correct in meaning and grammar, it is contrary to what is stated in the copies of the Qur’an of the Muslims, because in bala there is an additional ya’ in his readings which is not in the copies of the Qur’an, and despite that it is a reading that we do not know of any of the readers of the regions reciting it. As for the reading mentioned from Ibn Muhaisin, what Abu ʿAmr said about it is correct, because the Arabs confirm what comes after bal, they do not negate it, and the question in this case is one of denial, not confirmation.

c: This is because God has informed us
m: about the polytheists that they are in doubt about the Hour, as He said, “Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it.” The commentators differed in their interpretation of this.

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is: Rather, their knowledge will reach them in the Hereafter, so they will be certain of it when they witness it, while their certainty of it did not benefit them, as they were disbelievers in it in this world.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: Ata’ Al-Khurasani said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas Rather, their knowledge has overtaken them, he said: Their sight in the Hereafter when knowledge and sight will not benefit them.

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: Rather, their knowledge will be hidden in the Hereafter.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement Rather, their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter means their knowledge will be lost.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Rather, their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter, he said: He says: Their knowledge will be lost in the Hereafter, so they have no knowledge of it, they are blind to it.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: They did not have Surat al-Naml 27:66 Rather, their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter. Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it. any knowledge of it.
Who said that?

c: Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of my grandfather, he said: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Rather, their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter, he said: He used to recite it, Rather, their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter, he said: They did not attain knowledge of it, nor did they attain any desire for it.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Rather, he realized: or he realized.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid Rather, their knowledge has overtaken them, he said: Or has it overtaken them?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Uthman told us, on the authority of Mujahid Rather,
m: he overtook their knowledge, he said: Or did he overtook their knowledge? How can he overtook their knowledge?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

x: The most correct interpretation of this is based on the reading of those who read rather, they overcame the saying we mentioned on the authority of ʿAtaʿ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, which is that its meaning is: If it is read like this, and they do not know when they will be resurrected, rather their knowledge will overtake them at the same time in the Hereafter when they are resurrected, so their knowledge of it will not benefit them then. As for in this world, they are in doubt about it, rather they are blind to it. Rather, I said: This statement is the most correct interpretation of that according to the reading that you mentioned, because that is the most apparent of its meanings. And since that was its meaning, there was something omitted in the speech that was dispensed with by the indication of what appeared from it. That is because the meaning of the speech is: And they do not know when they will be resurrected, rather they know that in the Hereafter.

So if that is the meaning of the speech, and they do not know when they will be resurrected, rather their knowledge of that will be realized in the Hereafter, rather they are in doubt about it in this world.

i: As for the reading of those who read it as bal idrak with a kasra on the lam and a shaddah on the dal, then the statement that we mentioned from Mujahid is that the meaning of bal is am, and the Arabs place am in place of bal, and am in place of bal, if there is a question at the beginning of the speech, as the poet said:
x: I swear to God, I don't know if Aslami is crazy, or if I'm asleep, or if all my beloved has died.

He means by that, rather, all to a beloved, so the interpretation of the statement is: And they do not know when they will be resurrected, rather their knowledge will be made up in the Hereafter: meaning, their knowledge will be continued in the Hereafter: that is, with the knowledge of the Hereafter: that is, it will not be continued in that and they will not know it, rather their knowledge will be hidden from him, and it will go astray so they will not reach it or comprehend it. And His statement, Rather, they are in doubt about it, means: Rather, these polytheists who ask you about the Hour are in doubt about its occurrence, they are not certain of it, and they do not believe that they will be resurrected after death. Rather, they are blind to it, means: Rather, they are blind to the knowledge of its occurrence.

Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of my grandfather, he said: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Rather, their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter, he said: He used to recite it, Rather, their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter, he said: They did not attain knowledge of it, nor did they attain any desire for it.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct interpretation of this is based on the reading of those who read rather, they overcame the saying we mentioned on the authority of ʿAtaʿ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, which is that its meaning is: If it is read like this, and they do not know when they will be resurrected, rather their knowledge will overtake them at the same time in the Hereafter when they are resurrected, so their knowledge of it will not benefit them then.
