As for the reading of those who read it as bal idrak with a kasra on the lam and a shaddah on the dal, then the statement that we mentioned from Mujahid is that the meaning of bal is am, and the Arabs place am in place of bal, and am in place of bal, if there is a question at the beginning of the speech, as the poet said: I swear to God, I don't know if Aslami is crazy, or if I'm asleep, or if all my beloved has died.

x: God Almighty says: Those who disbelieved in God said, Shall we indeed be brought forth from our graves alive, as we were after our death, after we had been in them dust, having decayed?

This has been promised to us, we and our fathers before. He says: This has been promised to us before by Muhammad, and our fathers were promised this, but we did not see the truth of it, nor did we see its validity. This is nothing but legends of the ancients. He says: They said: This promise is nothing but what the ancients wrote of lies in their books, so they included it in them and spoke of it without it having any validity.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these deniers of the report you have brought them from your Lord: Travel through the land and observe the homes of those who came before you who denied God’s messengers and their dwellings, how they are. Did not God destroy them and destroy their people because they denied their messengers and rejected their advice, so that the homes were empty of them and the monuments and relics were obliterated? That was the consequence of their crime, and that is the way of your Lord with everyone who followed their path in denying the messengers of their Lord. God will do that to you if you do not hasten to repent from your disbelief and denial of the Messenger of your Lord.
And His statement,
h
And do not grieve over them

, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not grieve over the turning away of these polytheists from you and their denial of you. And do not be in distress over what they plot, meaning: Do not let your chest be constricted by their plotting against you, for God will support you against them and destroy them by the sword.

God Almighty says: And the polytheists of your people say, O Muhammad, who deny what you have brought them from your Lord, When will this promise of punishment that you have promised us be, which is for us in what you say is a state, if you are truthful in what you promise us? Say, ‘Perhaps there will be a punishment similar to that for you’ God Almighty says: Say to them, O Muhammad: Perhaps some of what you are hastening has drawn near to you and approached some of what you are hastening of God’s punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, Say, ‘Perhaps there will be a follower of yours,’ meaning: it will come near to you.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Say, ‘Perhaps some of what
h
you are hastening
will be followed by you.’ He says: Some of what
h
you are hastening
will be brought near to you.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Perhaps he will be a successor to you, he said: Successor means hasten to you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, Say, ‘Perhaps some of what you are impatient for will be followed by you.’ He said: It has come to an end.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, He has come close to you, that he has brought you closer. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the inclusion of the lam in the phrase radfa lakum He followed you. The well-known Arabic language is: radfahu a matter, and ardfahu, just as one says: taba’u and ataba’u.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He included the lam in that, and added the verb with it, just as one says li-lal-Ri’wah yu-tabirun (For the vision you interpret)
r
(Yusuf 12:43)
and li-Lil-Rabhum yarhabun (al-A’raf 7:154).

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: He included the lam in that for the meaning, because its meaning is: He approached them, as the poet said: I told her that things are brought to the young man So he inserted the letter ba in yatarhun they throw, and it is said tarahtuhu I threw him, because the meaning of tarah is throwing, so he inserted the letter ba for the meaning, since the meaning of that was that they throw the young man. This second statement is the more correct in my opinion, and the explanation has already been given in similar cases in other places in the book, which makes repeating it in this place unnecessary. And in a similar way to what we said about the meaning of His statement,
h
You are hastening
, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: Some of what
h
you are hastening
has been sent to you. He said: Of the punishment.

x: God Almighty says, And indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is full of bounty to mankind by not hastening to punish them for their disobedience to Him and their disbelief in Him, and is full of kindness to them in that and in other blessings He bestows upon them. But most of them do not give thanks for His kindness and bounty to them, so they devote worship to Him alone, but they associate with Him in worship that which harms them and does not benefit them, and that which has no bounty or kindness with them.

And His statement, And indeed, your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they declare, means: And indeed, your Lord knows the secrets in the hearts of His creation, and what is hidden in their souls, and what is hidden in their secrets, and what is apparent in their affairs. Nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He is recording it for them until He rewards all of them for good with good and for evil with its recompense. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told me, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: And indeed, your Lord knows what their hearts conceal. He said: The secret.

x: God Almighty says: There is nothing concealed or hidden in the heaven or on earth but that it is in a Book which is the Mother of the Book in which our Lord has established everything that will be from the time He began to create His creation until the Day of Resurrection. What He means by His statement made clear is that it makes clear to whoever looks at it and reads what our Lord, may He be glorified, has established in it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And there is nothing hidden in the heaven or the earth but that it is in a clear register
, meaning: There is nothing in the heaven or the earth, secret or public, but that He knows it.

x: And His statement, Indeed, this Qur'an narrates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they differ, God Almighty says: Indeed, this Qur'an that I have sent down to you, O Muhammad, narrates to the Children of Israel the truth in most of the things over which they differed, such as the matter over which they differed concerning Jesus. The Jews said what they said about it, and the Christians said what they said about it, and these were disavowed because of their differences concerning it, and those were disavowed from those, and other matters over which they differed. So God Almighty said to them: Indeed, this Qur'an narrates to you the truth regarding that over which you differed, so follow it and acknowledge what is in it, for it narrates to you the truth and guides you to the path of right guidance.

God Almighty says: Indeed, this Qur’an is guidance, meaning: a clarification from God, with which He clarifies the truth in the matters of religion in which His creation differed. And a mercy to the believers, meaning: a mercy to those who believe in it and act according to what is in it.

Indeed, your Lord will judge between them. He says: Your Lord will judge between those who differed among the Children of Israel with His judgment concerning them, so He will take revenge on those who are wrong among them, and will reward those who are righteous among them with the same punishment. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. He says: And your Lord is Exalted in Might in His revenge on those who are wrong among them and others, no one will be able to prevent Him from taking revenge on them if He takes revenge. He is the Knowing of the righteous and just among those who differed among the Children of Israel regarding what they differed over, and of the wrongdoers who have strayed from guidance among others.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “So entrust your affairs to God, O Muhammad, and trust in Him, for He is sufficient for you. “Indeed, you are upon the clear truth” for whoever contemplates it, thinks about what is in it with reason, and ponders it with understanding. It is the truth, unlike what the Jews and Christians who differed among the Children of Israel are upon, and unlike what the idolaters who denied you in what you brought them of the truth are upon. He says: So do not be saddened by the denial of those who denied you, and by the opposition of those who opposed you, and proceed with the command of your Lord with which He sent you.

And His statement, Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, means: O Muhammad, you cannot understand the truth from someone whose heart God has sealed and caused him to die, because God has sealed him from understanding it. And you do not make the deaf hear the call, means: You cannot make the one whose hearing God has made deaf to hear hear that. When they turn their backs, means: When they turn their backs on him, turning away from him, they do not hear him because the filth of disbelief has overcome their hearts. They do not listen to the truth, nor do they ponder it, nor do they pay attention to its speaker, but they turn away from it and deny speaking about it and listening to it.

The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it as Wa ma anta bahadi with a ya’ and an alif and adding it to the blind, meaning: You, O Muhammad, are not a guide to the blind from the truth from his misguidance. The majority of the Kufian reciters read it as Wa ma anta tahdi al-‘ami with a ta’ and the blind being in the accusative, meaning: You do not guide them from their misguidance, but God guides them if He wills. In my opinion, they are two readings with similar meanings, well-known among the reciters of the regions, so whichever one recites, the reciter is correct. The interpretation of the statement is as you have described: And you, O Muhammad, are not a guide for one whom God has blinded from guidance and right conduct, so He has put a veil over his sight, preventing him from distinguishing the path of right conduct from the misguidance he is in to the path of right conduct and the way of right conduct. And His statement:
h
You will not make anyone hear except he who believes in Our verses

means: You are not able to make anyone understand the truth and comprehend it except the one who believes in Our verses, meaning in His proofs, arguments, and verses of His revelation. They are Muslims for they hear what you say, ponder it, think about it, and act upon it, so they are the ones who hear.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of this.

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the Kufians read it as Wa ma anta bahadi with a ya’ and an alif and adding it to the blind, meaning: You, O Muhammad, are not a guide to the blind from the truth from his misguidance.

The majority of the Kufian reciters read it as Wa ma anta tahdi al-‘ami with a ta’ and the blind being in the accusative, meaning: You do not guide them from their misguidance, but God guides them if He wills.
In my opinion, they are two readings with similar meanings, well-known among the reciters of the regions, so whichever one recites, the reciter is correct.

x: Mention of those who said the same as we said about the Almighty’s saying occurred:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And when the word comes to pass against them
, he said: It is true against them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And when the word comes to pass against them
, meaning: when the word is due upon them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: The word fell upon them, he said: the right of punishment. Ibn Jurayj said: The saying: the torment.

x: Mention of those who said our saying in the meaning of the saying:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And when the word falls upon them and the word means anger.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Hafsa, who said:
m: I asked Abu al-Aaliyah about His statement,
h
And when the word comes to pass against them
, so he said: God revealed to Noah, None of your people will believe except those who have already believed
r
. She said: It was as if there had been a cover over my face and then it was removed.

x: A group of scholars said: The emergence of this beast that he mentioned will happen when people do not command what is right and forbid what is wrong.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Amr ibn Qays, on the authority of Atiyyah al-Awfi, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And when the word comes to pass against them
, We will produce for them a creature from the earth, he said: It is when they do not enjoin what is right nor forbid what is wrong.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Muhammad bin Al-Hasan Abu Al-Hasan told us, he said: Amr bin Qais Al-Mala’i told us, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And when the word comes to pass against them
, We will produce for them a creature from the earth, he said: That is when enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is abandoned.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Qays, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: regarding his statement,
h
We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them
, he said: When they do not enjoin what is right, nor forbid what is wrong.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr al-Maqdisi told me: Ash’ath ibn Abdullah al-Sijistani told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Atiyyah,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And when the word comes to pass against them

, We will produce for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them, he said: If they do not recognize what is right and do not denounce what is wrong. He mentioned that the land from which the beast will emerge is Mecca.

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Al-Ashja’i told me, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzuq, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said:
m: The beast will emerge from a crack in Al-Safa like a horse galloping for three days, and a third of it will not emerge. Ibn Hamid narrated: Al-Hakam bin Bashir narrated: Amr bin Qais narrated: Al-Furat Al-Qazzaz narrated: Amir bin Wathilah Abi At-Tufayl narrated: Hudhayfah bin Asid Al-Ghifari said: When the Beast emerges, some people will see it and say: By God, we have seen the Beast, until it reaches that Imam and he is pursued but cannot do anything. Then it emerges and the people will see it and say: By God, we have seen it, until it reaches that Imam and he is pursued but cannot do anything. Then it will say: When the one who mentions it speaks, he said: Until killing is counted for it. Then it emerges, and when the people see it, they will enter the mosque to pray, and it will come to them and say: Now you are praying! Then it will cut off the nose of the disbeliever and wipe the forehead of the Muslim with a forelock. Then the people will live a time and say: This one is a believer and this one is a Surat al-Naml 27:82
h
And when the word comes to pass against them
, We will produce for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them, that mankind was not certain of Our signs. disbeliever.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Uthman bin Matar narrated to us, on the authority of Wasil,
m: the freed slave of Abu Uyaynah, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, on the authority of Hudhayfah and Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qays bin Saʿd, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, on the authority of Hudhayfah bin Asid, regarding His statement, We will bring forth for them a beast from the earth that will speak to them, he said: The beast will have three emergences: one in some desert, then it will lie in wait; one in some village when the rulers shed blood there, then it will lie in wait. While the people are at the most honorable, greatest, and best of mosques, the earth will rise above them, and the people will flee, leaving a group of believers, saying, Nothing can save us from God. Then the beast will come out to them, shining their faces like a shining star, then it will set out, and no seeker will catch up with it, and no fugitive will escape it. It will come to a man who is praying, and he will say, By God, I was not one of the people of prayer, and he will turn to it, and it will crush him. He said, It will polish the face of the believer and crush the face of the disbeliever. We said, What will happen to the people at that time? He said: Neighbors in the neighborhood, partners in money, and companions in travel.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Jami’, on the authority of Abd Al-Malik bin Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Baylamani, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: People go to a gathering at night, and the beast of the earth goes to them at night, and they wake up with its head and tail covering them. There is no believer but it wipes him out, and no disbeliever or hypocrite but it tramples him.

c: Mujahid bin Musa told us: Yazid told us: Al-Khaibari told us, on the authority of Hayyan bin Umair, on the authority of Hassan bin Hamsa, who said:
m: I heard Abdullah bin Amr say: If I wanted, I could wear these sandals of mine, and I would not touch the ground while sitting until I stood on the stones from between which the beast would emerge, and it was as if I saw it emerging in the wake of a group of pilgrims. He said: I have never performed Hajj without fearing that it would emerge in our wake.

c: Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Amili told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Qais ibn Saʿd, on the authority of Ataʿ, who said:
m: I saw Abdullah ibn Amr, whose house was close to al-Safa, raise his foot while standing, and say: If I wanted, I would not put it down until I put it down on the place from which the Beast will emerge. Issam bin Rawad bin Al Jarrah narrated: My father narrated: Sufyan bin Saeed Al Thawri narrated: Mansour bin Al Mu'tamir narrated: Rib'i bin Harash narrated: I heard Hudhayfah bin Al Yaman say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “And he mentioned the Beast, and Hudhayfah said: I said, O Messenger of God, from where will it emerge? He said: ‘From the most sacred mosques to God, while Jesus is circumambulating the House with the Muslims, the earth shakes beneath them, shaking the lamp, and the Safa splits apart near the Mas'a, and the Beast emerges from the Safa, its head as soon as it appears, polished, with fur and feathers. No seeker will catch up with it, and no fugitive will escape it. It will mark people as believer and disbeliever. As for the believer, it will leave his face like a shining star, and it will write between his eyes, ‘Believer.’ As for the disbeliever, it will make a black dot between his eyes, ‘Disbeliever.’”

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hussein narrated to us, saying: Abu Al-Hussein narrated to us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid bin Jud’an, on the authority of Aws bin Khalid, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The beast will emerge with the seal of Solomon and the staff of Moses, and it will polish the face of the believer with the staff and seal the nose of the unbeliever with the seal, until the people of the house will gather and one of them will say, ‘O believer,’ and another will say, ‘O unbeliever.’” He said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said:

c: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It is a creature with fur and feathers, and it has four legs. It emerges from some of the valleys of Tihamah. He said: Abdullah ibn Umar said: It makes a black mark on the face of the disbeliever, and it spreads over his face, and his face turns black. And it makes a white mark on the face of the believer, and it spreads over his face, until his face turns white. Then the people of the house sit at the table and they know the believer from the disbeliever, and they trade in the markets, and they know the believer from the disbeliever.

c: Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Ibn Lahi’ah and Yahya ibn Ayoub told us: Ibn al-Haad told us, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Hakam,
m: that he heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: The beast will emerge from a ravine, and its head will touch the clouds, but its feet will remain on the ground until they emerge. It will pass by a person praying and will say: What is prayer for you? So it will snatch his nose from its mouth.

c: Salih bin Mismar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Fadik narrated to us, saying: Yazid bin Ayyad narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq,
m: that it reached him on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The beast of the earth will emerge, and with it will be the ring of Solomon and the staff of Moses. As for the unbeliever, it will be sealed between his eyes with the ring of Solomon, and as for the believer, it will wipe his face with the staff of Moses and it will turn white. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, talk to them. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it as talk to them with a damma on the ta’ and a shaddah on the lam, meaning you inform them and talk to them. Abu Zur’ah ibn Amr read it as talk to them with a fatha on the ta’ and a shaddah on the lam, meaning you name them. The reading that I do not permit other than that is what the readers of the countries do. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them
, he said: It will speak to them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
We brought forth for them a creature from the earth that spoke to them
, and in some readings it speaks to them, saying to them,
h
That the people were not certain of Our signs

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, She speaks to them, he said: Her speech informs them,
h
that the people were not certain of Our signs
. And his saying,
h
That the people were not certain of Our signs

, the reciters differed in their recitation of that, so the majority of the people close to the Hijaz, Basra, and Syria recited it as that the people with a kasra on the alif of that as a way of beginning with the report about the people that they were not certain of the signs of God, and even though it is kasra in the recitation of these people, the speech is addressed to it, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the people of Basra recited it as that the people were with a fatha on that meaning: He spoke to them that the people, so it is then in the accusative case because the speech falls on it. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two readings with similar meanings and are widespread in the readings of the regions, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, talk to them.
The majority of the reciters of the regions read it as talk to them with a damma on the ta’ and a shaddah on the lam, meaning you inform them and talk to them.
Abu Zur’ah ibn Amr read it as talk to them with a fatha on the ta’ and a shaddah on the lam, meaning you name them.
The reading that I do not permit other than that is what the readers of the countries do.

And his saying, That the people were not certain of Our signs, the reciters differed in their recitation of that, so the majority of the people close to the Hijaz, Basra, and Syria recited it as that the people with a kasra on the alif of that as a way of beginning with the report about the people that they were not certain of the signs of God, and even though it is kasra in the recitation of these people, the speech is addressed to it, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the people of Basra recited it as that the people were with a fatha on that meaning: He spoke to them that the people, so it is then in the accusative case because the speech falls on it.
The correct thing to say about this is that they are two readings with similar meanings and are widespread in the readings of the regions, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.

x: God Almighty says: And the Day We will gather from every century and religion a group, meaning a group of them, and a group of those who deny Our signs meaning: of those who deny Our proofs and arguments, then He will detain the first of them over the last of them, so that they will all gather, then they will be driven to the Fire. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And the Day We shall gather from every nation a group of those who denied Our signs
, and they will be driven in ranks, meaning: the Shi’a at the gathering.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, From every nation a group, he said: a group.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
We will gather from every nation a group
, he said: Group after group, and they will be distributed.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Those who deny Our signs will be driven back, he said: He says: They will be pushed back.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, So they are distributed, he said: The first of them will be detained for the last of them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They will be distributed. He said: He distributed it, the first of them will be returned to the last of them. I have explained the meaning of his saying they distribute previously with its evidence, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.

x: And His statement, Until, when they come, He will say, ‘Did you deny My signs?’ God Almighty says: Until, when there comes from every nation a group of those who deny Our signs and gather together, God says, Did you deny My signs? That is, My proofs and evidence. And you did not encompass them with knowledge? That is, and you did not know them as they should be known. What were you doing? in them of denying or believing.

God Almighty says: And the wrath and anger of God are due to those who deny His signs because of their wrongdoing meaning because of their denial of God’s signs, on the Day they are gathered so they will not speak meaning: they will not speak with an argument to defend themselves from the enormity of what has befallen them and what has been said to them.
And His statement,
h
Have they not seen that We made the night for them to rest in

? God Almighty says: Have these deniers of Our signs not seen Our alternation of night and day, and Our difference between them by making this a resting place for them in which they rest, and rest their bodies from the fatigue of moving and turning during the day, and this a light in which they see and witness things and turn in it for their livelihoods, so they reflect on that, and ponder, and know that the Disposer of that is thus God, for whom nothing is incapable, and it is not difficult for Him to cause the death of the living, and to bring the dead back to life after death, just as it is not difficult for Him to take away the day and bring the night, and to bring the day and take away the night despite the difference in their conditions. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe. God Almighty says: Indeed in Our making the night a place of rest, and the day a place of sight, there is evidence for a people who believe in God of His ability to do what they believe in regarding resurrection after death, and an argument for them on the Oneness of God.

The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of the Almighty’s saying, And on the Day the Trumpet is blown. We have mentioned their differences previously, and we have explained the correct statement in this regard according to us with its evidence. However, we will mention in this place some of the reports that were not mentioned there.
Some of them said: It is a horn that will be blown into.
Some of those who were not mentioned before mentioned in the report about that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And the Day the Trumpet is blown
, he said, It is like a trumpet.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The trumpet is the trumpet. He said: It is the trumpet whose owner is holding it, grasping two handfuls with his hands on the end of the horn, between its end and his mouth, the size of a handful or thereabouts. He has knelt on the knee of one of his legs, so he pointed, so he knelt on the knee of his left leg, squatting on its foot, its heel under his thigh, his buttocks and the tips of his toes in the dirt. He said: Al-Hussein told us, he said:

c: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdullah, he said:
m: The trumpet is in the form of a horn, raising one of its knees to the sky and lowering the other. Its eyelids have not slept since God created the heavens, ready and eager. The trumpet has been placed on its mouth, waiting for when it will be commanded to blow into it.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharbi narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’ al-Madani,
m: on the authority of Yazid ibn Ziyad (Abu Ja’far said: The correct version is Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad), on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: He said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Messenger of God, what is the Trumpet? He said: A horn. He said: And how is it? He said: “A great horn in which three blasts will be blown: the first: the blast of terror, the second: the blast of fainting, and the third: the blast of rising for God, Lord of the worlds. God commands Israfil with the first blast, and he says: ‘Blow the blast of terror.’ So he blows the blast of terror, and the inhabitants of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth are terrified, except for whom God wills. God commands him to prolong it and lengthen it, and he does not slacken. It is the one about which God says: ‘These people do not wait except for a single blast, which will have no stopping.’”
r
(Surah Sad: 15)
. Then God moves the mountains, and they become a mirage, and the earth shakes with its inhabitants. Raja, which is what God says:
h
The Day the violent earthquake will shake, * Followed by the second earthquake, * Hearts that Day will be trembling

(al-Nazi’at 79:6-8). The earth will be like a ship tied down in the sea, battered by the waves, toppling over with its people, or like a lantern suspended by a string, swayed by the winds, causing people to sway on its back, so nursing mothers will be startled, pregnant women will give birth, children will turn gray, and the devils will fly away, fleeing until they reach the regions, and the angels will meet them, striking their faces, and they will return, and people will turn back, calling out to one another. It is what God says:
h
The Day of Calling, * The Day you will turn back, fleeing. You will have no protector from God. And whomsoever God sends astray, for him there is no guide
r

. While they were like that, the earth cracked from one country to another, and they saw a tremendous thing, and it seized them with a distress that only God knows about. Then they looked at the sky, and behold, it was like molten molten metal. Then its sun and moon were eclipsed, and its stars were scattered, then it was removed from them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: And the dead do not know anything about that. Abu Hurairah said: O Messenger of God, who did God except when He says, ‘So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth is terrified,
h
except whom God wills

’? He said: “Those are the martyrs, and terror only reaches the living. They are alive with their Lord, receiving provision. God has protected them from the terror of that Day and made them safe, and it is the punishment of God which He sends upon the worst of His creation.”

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ismail bin Rafi’ narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God, the Blessed and Exalted, finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the trumpet and gave it an angel. He placed it on his mouth, staring at the Throne, waiting for when he would be commanded. I said: O Messenger of God, what is the trumpet? He said: A horn. I said: How is it? He said: Great. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, its greatness is a circle within it, as wide as the heavens and the earth. He commands it, and it blows the blast of terror, and the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth are terrified, except for whom God wills.” Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith similar to the hadith of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Al-Maharibi, except that he said in his hadith: Like a ship anchored in the sea.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: And He blows the trumpet of creation.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And the Day the Trumpet is blown means in creation
. His statement,
h
Then those in the heavens and those on the earth will be terrified
means: Those in the heavens of the angels and those on the earth of the jinn, mankind, and devils will be terrified by the horror of what they will witness on that Day.

x: How is it said: Fazaa'a, making Fazaa'a, which is a verb, attributed to yanfakh, and it is yaf'ala?

The Arabs do that in places where ifa is suitable, because ifa is suitable with fa'ala and yaf'ala, like when you say: I visit you if you visit me, and I visit you if you visit me. So if if is put in place of ifa, it is treated like ifa.
Then where is the answer to his statement:
h
And the Day the Trumpet is blown
, then yaf'a will be terrified?

It is permissible for it to be implied with the waw, as if it was said: And the word will fall upon them for what they did wrong, so they will not speak, and that is the Day the Trumpet is blown. It is permissible for it to be left out, and the indication of the speech to it from it is sufficient, as it was said: And if those who did wrong could see Al-Baqarah 2:165, so its answer was left out. And His saying,
h
Except whom God wills

, it was said: Those whom God has excluded in this place from being struck by terror on that Day are the martyrs, and that is because they are alive with their Lord and are provided for, even if they are counted among the dead among the people of this world. This is what was reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we mentioned it in the previous report.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Al-Awam told us, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Abu Hurairah,
m: that he recited this verse: So everyone in the heavens and on the earth was terrified, except whom God willed. He said: They are the martyrs. And his saying, And all of them came to Him in humiliation, means: And all of them came to Him in a state of humiliation. And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And all will come to Him in humiliation
, meaning: in a state of humiliation.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they all came to Him in humiliation. He said: Subdued.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And all will come to Him in humiliation

, he said: The humble one is the one who is humbled and subdued. He said: Because the person who is frightened when he is frightened only wants to escape from the matter that frightened him. He said: So when the trumpet was blown, they were terrified, and there was no escape for them from God. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement,
h
And all of them will come to Him in humiliation
. The majority of reciters in the regions read it,
h
And all of them will come to Him in humiliation

, with the extension of the alif of atawah in the form of fa’iluhu, except for Ibn Mas’ud, who read it, And all of them will come to Him in the form of fa’iluhu. The later reciters, Al-A’mash and Hamzah, followed him in reading it this way. Those who read it in the form of fa’iluhu considered it weak due to the consensus of the reciters regarding His statement,
h
And all of them will come to Him Maryam 19

:95. They said: So too is His statement, they came to Him in the plural. As for those who read according to the reading of Abdullah, they rejected it based on His statement, So he was terrified, as if they directed the meaning of the statement to: And on the Day the Trumpet is blown, everyone in the heavens and the earth will be terrified, and they will come to Him all in humiliation, as is said in speech: He saw, fled, and returned, humiliated. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two widely used readings in the regions, and they have similar meanings, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.

evidence.text: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Al-Awam told us, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that he recited this verse: So everyone in the heavens and on the earth was terrified, except whom God willed.
The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, And all of them will come to Him in humiliation.

The majority of reciters in the regions read it, And all of them will come to Him in humiliation, with the extension of the alif of atawah in the form of fa’iluhu, except for Ibn Mas’ud, who read it, And all of them will come to Him in the form of fa’iluhu.
The later reciters, Al-A’mash and Hamzah, followed him in reading it this way.
Those who read it in the form of fa’iluhu considered it weak due to the consensus of the reciters regarding His statement, And all of them will come to Him Maryam 19:95.

As for those who read according to the reading of Abdullah, they rejected it based on His statement, So he was terrified, as if they directed the meaning of the statement to: And on the Day the Trumpet is blown, everyone in the heavens and the earth will be terrified, and they will come to Him all in humiliation, as is said in speech: He saw, fled, and returned, humiliated.

x: God Almighty says: And you see the mountains, O Muhammad, and you think they are standing, while they are passing by.

c: Like what Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And you will see the mountains and think them rigid

, meaning: standing. And it was only said, And they will pass like the passing of clouds, because they are gathered and then move, so the one who sees them will think, because of their large number, that they are standing still, while they are moving quickly, as Al-Ja’di said: They are so reckless, like mountains, you think they are stopping for a pilgrim, while the passengers are neglecting them. His saying, The creation of God,
h
who perfected everything
and strengthened His creation. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
The work of God
, who perfected all things, means: He perfected all things.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
The work of God
, who perfected all things, meaning: He perfected and strengthened all things that He created.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Who perfected everything
, he said: He made everything secure and perfected.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Atqan means more trustworthy.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada He is All-Knowing of what they do God Almighty says:
m: God is All-Knowing of what His servants do of good and evil, obedience to Him and disobedience to Him, and He will reward all of them for all of that, for good with good, and for evil with evil like it.

x: God Almighty says: Whoever comes to God with His Oneness and belief in Him, and saying, There is no god but God, with his heart certain of it, will have from this good deed with God good on the Day of Resurrection, and that good is that God will reward him from it Paradise, and will protect him from the terror of the Great Blast, which is the blowing of the Trumpet.
h
And whoever brings evil

means: whoever brings associating partners with Him on the Day he meets Him, and denying His Oneness, their faces will be covered with dust in the fire of Hell. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Khalaq al-Asqalani told me: Al-Fadl ibn Dukayn told me: Yahya ibn Ayyub al-Bajali told us:
m: I heard Abu Zur’ah say: Abu Hurayrah said - Yahya said: I think it was on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - he said:
h
Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it

, and they, from the terror of that Day, will be safe. He said: It is there is no god but God. “And whoever brings an evil deed, their faces will be thrown down into the Fire.” He said: It is polytheism.

c: Musa bin Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to us, saying: Abu Yahya al-Hammani narrated to us, on the authority of al-Nadr bin Arabi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it

, and they, from the terror of that Day, will be safe, he said: Whoever brings there is no god but God, “and whoever brings an evil deed, their faces will be thrown down into the Fire,” he said: with polytheism.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it
, meaning: whoever brings there is no god but God, “and whoever brings an evil deed,” which is polytheism.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever brings evil
, he said: polytheism.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Whoever brings a good deed
, he said: the word of sincerity, and whoever brings an evil deed, he said: polytheism.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: in a similar manner. Ibn Jurayj said: I heard Ata’ say that it includes polytheism, meaning in His statement,
h
And whoever brings evil

c: Ibn Hamid told us:
m: He said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Muhajjil, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: He used to swear an oath without exception, that
h
whoever brings a good deed
he said: There is no god but God, and whoever brings an evil deed he said: polytheism.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’,
m: similarly.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said: Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b,
m: h
And whoever brings evil
- their faces will be thrown into the Fire. He said: Polytheism.

c: Abu Al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Hafs narrated to us, saying: Sa'id bin Sa'id narrated to us, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussein,
m: who was a warrior, who said: While he was in one of his private moments, he raised his voice, "There is no god but God alone, with no partner for Him. His is the dominion and His is the praise. He gives life and causes death. In His hand is good, and He has power over all things." A man replied to him, What do you say, O servant of God? He said, I say what you hear. He said, It is the word of which God said, '
h
Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it
, and they, from the terror of that Day, will be safe.'

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
h
Whoever brings a good deed
he said:
m: sincerity. And whoever brings an evil deed he said: polytheism.
b.via: Whoever brings a good deed he

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, regarding His statement,
h
And whoever brings evil
, meaning: polytheism.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: h
And whoever brings evil
: he says: polytheism.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
And whoever brings evil
- their faces will be thrown into the Fire. He said: Evil: polytheism and disbelief.

c: Saad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me: Hafs bin Omar Al-Adani told us: Al-Hakam bin Iban told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Whoever brings a good deed
, he said: The testimony that there is no god but God. And whoever brings an evil deed, he said: The evil deed is polytheism. Al-Hakam said: Ikrimah said: Everything in the Qur’an Surat al-Naml 27:90
h
And whoever brings evil

- their faces will be thrown into the Fire. Are you recompensed except for what you used to do? that is an evil deed is polytheism. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of His statement,
h
He will have something better than her
, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He will have something better than it, so from it goodness reached him, Ibn Abbas meant by that from the good deed goodness reached the one who brought it.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Ruh bin Ubadah told us: Husayn al-Shahid told us, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: h
Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it
. He said: He will have better than it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: Whoever says there is no god but God, will have something better than it.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, Then
h
he will have something better than her
, meaning: he will have a share of her.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it
. He said: He will have better than it. As for it being better than faith, no, but there is good from it and he will attain good from it.

c: Saad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told us: Hafs bin Omar told us: Al-Hakam told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it
, meaning: There is nothing better than There is no god but God, but he will have better than it. Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it
, he said: God gave him ten for one, so this is better than it. The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase
h
And they will be safe from the terror of that Day

x: Some of the reciters from Basra read it as
h
And they will be safe from the terror of that Day
by adding terror to the day.

A group of the reciters from Kufa read it as From the terror of that Day with the tanween of terror. What is correct in my opinion regarding this matter is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions and are close in meaning, so whichever one the reader recites is correct. However, the addition is more pleasing to me because it is a known fear. If that is the case, then it is definite, given that it is in the context of His statement, And the Day the Trumpet is blown, then whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom God wills. If that is the case, then it is known that what He meant by His statement,
h
And they will be safe from the terror of that Day
, is the terror that was mentioned before it. If that is the case, then there is no doubt that it is definite, and that the addition, if it is definite, is better than leaving the addition.

Another is that if it is added, then it is more clear that it is report of safety from all the terrors of that Day than if it was not added, because if it was not added, it would most likely have made safety from the terror of some of its terrors. And His statement, Are you recompensed for anything other than what you used to do? God Almighty says: It will be said to them: Are you recompensed, O polytheists, for anything other than what you used to do, when God threw you face down into the Fire, or for what you used to do in this world that angered your Lord? And He left it said to them, as the speech was sufficient to indicate it.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase And they will be safe from the terror of that Day.
Some of the reciters from Basra read it as And they will be safe from the terror of that Day by adding terror to the day.
A group of the reciters from Kufa read it as From the terror of that Day with the tanween of terror.
What is correct in my opinion regarding this matter is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions and are close in meaning, so whichever one the reader recites is correct.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, say, I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, which is Mecca, who has made it sacred to His creation, that they should not shed forbidden blood therein, or wrong anyone therein, or hunt its game, or be alone within it without the idols that you, O polytheists, worship. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city who has made it sacred

, meaning: Mecca. And His statement, And to Him belongs everything, means: And to the Lord of this city belongs all things, so I have been commanded to worship Him, not someone who owns nothing. Rather, God, the Most High, said, The Lord of this city who has made it sacred, and He mentioned it specifically and not all other cities, even though He is the Lord of all cities, because He wanted to inform the polytheists among the people of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), who are the people of Mecca, of His blessings and kindness to them, and that the One they should worship is the One who made their city sacred, and prevented people from them, while they are in all other cities eating and killing each other, not someone who has not bestowed blessings upon them and is not able to benefit or harm them. And His statement,
h
And I have been commanded to be of the Muslims

, means: And my Lord has commanded me to submit my face to Him, inclining toward truth, so I will be of the Muslims who follow the religion of His friend Abraham and your grandfather, O polytheists, not someone who opposes the religion of his true grandfather and follows the religion of Satan, the enemy of God.

x: God Almighty says: Say: I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city and “to be of the Muslims * and to recite the Qur’an. So whoever is guided” means: whoever follows me and believes in me and what I have brought, and takes the path of righteousness is only guided for himself means: he only takes the path of righteousness by following me, believing in me, and in what I have brought for himself, because by his belief in me and in what I have brought he is safe from His vengeance in this world and His punishment in the Hereafter. And His statement,
h
And whoever has gone astray

, meaning: And whoever has deviated from the right path by denying Me and what I have brought from God, Say, ‘I am only one of the warners,’ meaning: God Almighty says: So say, O Muhammad, to whoever has gone astray from the right path, and denied you, and did not believe in what I have brought from Me, I am only one who warns his people of the punishment of God and His wrath for their disobedience to Him. And I have warned you of that, O group of disbelievers of Quraysh. So if you accept and desist from what God hates from you of associating partners with Him, then you will attain your own good, but if you reject and deny, then you have sinned against yourselves. And I have conveyed to you what I was commanded to convey to you, and I have given you sincere advice.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those polytheists of your people who say to you, When will this promise come to pass, if you should be truthful? “Praise be to God” for His blessing upon us by guiding us to the truth from which you are blind. Your Lord will show you the signs of His punishment and His wrath, and by them you will know the truth of My advice to you, and the truth of the guidance to which I have called you will become clear. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
He will show you His signs
, and you will recognize them, he said: In yourselves, and in the heavens, the earth, and provision.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
He will show you His signs
, and you will recognize them, he said: In yourselves, the heavens, the earth, and provision. And His statement,
h
And your Lord is not unaware of what you do

, means that God Almighty says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, is not unaware of what these polytheists do, but they have a term which they will reach, and when they reach it, they will not delay it an hour, nor will they advance it. God Almighty says to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Do not be saddened by their denial of you, for I am behind their destruction, and I am lying in wait for them. So be certain of victory for yourself, and of humiliation and disgrace for your enemy.

notes.en: T2 adds after it: “his statement.” The report’s source citation was given above, 1:207 and 17:542.
notes.ar: بعده في ت 2: "قوله". والأثر تقدم تخريجه في 1/ 207، 17/ 542.

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.en: M and T1 read: “a way.”
notes.ar: في م، ت 1: "سبيل".

notes.en: Omitted in Ṣ, T1, T2, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف.

notes.en: T2 reads: “they give.”
notes.ar: في ت 2: "يؤتون".

notes.en: See the preceding discussion at 1:611–612 and 2:198.
notes.ar: ينظر ما تقدم في 1/ 611، 612، 2/ 198.

notes.en: Omitted in M, T1, and F.
notes.ar: سقط من: م، ت 1، ف.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, and F read: “they disobeyed him.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "عصوه".

notes.en: M reads: “al-awkasūhā” (a variant reading).
notes.ar: في م: "الأوكسوها".

notes.en: A zand is a stick used to strike fire. “His zand became aṣlad” means that it made a sound but produced no fire. See al-Tāj, roots z-n-d and ṣ-l-d.
notes.ar: الزند: هو العود الذي يقدح به النار. وأصلد زنده، أي: صوَّت ولم يخرج نارًا. التاج (ز ن د، ص ل د).

notes.en: This is the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿĀmir. See Ibn Mujāhid, al-Sabʿa, p. 478.
notes.ar: هي قراءة ابن كثير ونافع وأبي عمرو وابن عامر. السبعة لابن مجاهد ص 478.

notes.en: This is the reading of ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī. See the same source.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr 9:2857 through al-Aʿmash. al-Bukhārī also transmitted it from Abū Nuʿaym, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥakam, as his statement; from Wakīʿ, from al-Aʿmash, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥakam, from Nawf; and from ʿAbdān, from Abū Ḥamza, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Walīd ibn al-Ḥakam, from Nawf. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5:104 to Ibn Abī Shayba and Ibn al-Mundhir. The phrase “like wolves” appeared in the printed text as “like flies.” Both are transmitted readings, as al-Suyūṭī notes. Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr 5:194 has “like wolves,” then says: “This is how I saw it vocalized, with a yāʾ, but it should have a bāʾ; that is a scribal error.”

notes.en: The verb yaftakū is used with the nūn omitted, without subjunctive or jussive marking; this is a recognized and correct Arabic usage. An example is the Prophet’s saying: “You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another.” Imām al-Nawawī notes that the nūn is omitted in “you believe” as a known, correct usage. See Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim with al-Nawawī’s commentary 2:36.
notes.ar: قوله: يفتكوا. بحذف النون دون نصب أو جزم لغة معروفة صحيحة، من ذلك قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تدخلون الجنة حتى تؤمنوا، ولا تؤمنوا حتى تحابوا". قال الإمام النووى: "ولا تؤمنوا"، بحذف النون من آخره وهى لغة معروفة صحيحة. صحيح مسلم بشرح النووى 2/ 36.

notes.en: F adds: “This is the end of the third part; the beginning of Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ follows at the start of the fourth part. It was completed on blessed Wednesday, the last day of blessed Shawwāl, in the year 1147 AH (1744/45 CE), by the servant most in need of God, Salāma ibn al-Ḥājj Salāma ibn al-Ḥājj Ḥijāzī Ḍayf Allāh al-Sindanhūrī. May God forgive him, his parents, his master, and whoever finds and corrects an error in it, and all Muslims. Amen, amen, amen. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. Finished.” This is the end of the copy available to us.
notes.ar: في ف: "وهو آخر الجزء الثالث يتلوه في أول الجزء الرابع أول سورة القصص، وكان الفراغ منه يوم الأربعاء المبارك سلخ شوال المبارك سنة 1147 ألف ومائة وسبعة وأربعين على يد أفقر العباد إلى الله تعالى سلامة بن الحاج سلامة بن الحاج حجازى ضيف الله السندنهورى، غفر الله له ولوالديه ولمالكه ولمن نظر فيه عيبا وأصلحه والجميع المسلمين آمين آمين آمين والحمد لله رب العالمين، تم". وهذا آخر الموجود عندنا من هذه. النسخة.
